  retry semantics, or idempotence keys.

  incidental implementation state inside the capability instead of exposing

  inline overflow/size reconciliation.

legal boundary and handler effect. Run relevant project typecheck, tests, and
lint/format checks; give exact commands and outcomes. Do not claim that a stub,
static check, or local test verifies live Engine behavior. If live Engine
verification needs separately configured infrastructure, say so.

Before reporting, inspect the complete diff for secrets, unrelated changes, and
behavior changes. Give a rollback path naming the precise changed files and
reversal steps. If checks fail, report the failures rather than describing them
as passed; do not broaden scope to silence them.

## Report

Return observed versions and behavior, changed files and bounded implementation,
test coverage, exact verification results, Connector/credential and state/effect
ownership review, live-service limitations, and rollback instructions. Distinguish
verified facts from unresolved assumptions.

# @maelstrom-co/react [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/maelstrom-co/maelstrom/blob/main/LICENSE) React bindings for Maelstrom — AI-orchestrated dynamic UIs. 📚 **Full documentation:** ## Install ```bash bun add @maelstrom-co/react ``` Or: `npm install` / `pnpm add` / `yarn add @maelstrom-co/react` ## What it does - **`createMaelstrom({ vessels })`** — factory that returns a typed Maelstrom instance — see bullets below for what it exposes - **`defineVessel(config)`** — declares the framework-agnostic vessel state machine - **`vessel(definition, component | loader, loadingComponent?)`** — pairs a vessel definition with a React component; `loadingComponent` is only used when a lazy loader is passed - **`WebSocketConnector` / `HttpConnector`** — client connectors re-exported for React apps - **`m.Provider`** — connects to the engine and owns all chart state; accepts any `EngineConnector` - **`m.Chart`** — renders the grid canvas; the engine emits layout directives that Chart renders as CSS positioning - **Hooks** - `useMaelstrom` — intent submission and connection status - `useVessel` and `useActions` — vessel-level state - `useInstance` — raw access to the Maelstrom instance - **`.with(extension)`** — builder for optional extensions ## Quick example ```tsx import { createMaelstrom, defineVessel, vessel, WebSocketConnector } from '@maelstrom-co/react'; const greetingVessel = vessel( defineVessel({ id: 'greeting', name: 'Greeting', description: 'Displays a greeting message.', defaultVariant: 'compact', variants: { compact: { description: 'One-line greeting', props: { message: 'Hello!' }, minSize: { width: 2, height: 1 }, actions: [], }, }, }), ({ variantProps }) =>
{variantProps.message}
); const m = createMaelstrom({ vessels: [greetingVessel] }); const connector = new WebSocketConnector({ url: 'ws://localhost:3001/ws' }); export function App() { return ( ); } ``` ## Docs - Quick start: https://docs.maelstrom-ai.co/getting-started/quick-start/ - Core concepts: https://docs.maelstrom-ai.co/getting-started/core-concepts/ - React guides: https://docs.maelstrom-ai.co/guides/react/creating-vessels/ - API reference: https://docs.maelstrom-ai.co/reference/react/readme/ ## License MIT

For APIs used, I inspected the installed React package README and declaration files for `createMaelstrom`, `vessel`, provider props, and typed vessel component props; installed protocol declarations for `defineVessel` and Vessel shapes; and read the checksummed read-only SDK source for `createMaelstrom`, `vessel`, protocol Vessel definitions and SDK tests. They verify sole registration/no Actions, disabled empty submit and delegation with the submitted query, pending/disabled rendering followed by success, and error feedback/re-enabled button on rejection. Search is mocked at the application-owned boundary; no external request is made.
